intro: The Key Pair Generator creates RSA and EC (ECDSA) key pairs and outputs them in PEM format directly in your browser using the Web Crypto API. It supports RSA-2048, RSA-4096, EC P-256, and EC P-384, returning a matching public and private key you can copy or download. It's handy when you need a quick keypair for testing, prototyping signing flows, or setting up local development credentials.
useCases: Generate an RSA or ECDSA keypair for testing JWT or token signing locally
Create a PEM public/private key pair for prototyping authentication flows
Produce EC P-256 or P-384 keys for ECDSA signature experiments
Get a quick RSA-2048 or RSA-4096 keypair without installing OpenSSL
Generate disposable keys for local development and integration tests

faq.q: Is my key data sent to a server?
faq.a: No. Key generation runs entirely in your browser via the Web Crypto API, and the generated keys never leave your device or get uploaded anywhere.

faq.q: Which algorithms and key sizes are supported?
faq.a: You can generate RSA keys (RSA-2048 or RSA-4096, using RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5 with SHA-256) and EC keys (P-256 or P-384, using ECDSA).

faq.q: What output format are the keys in?
faq.a: Keys are exported as PEM text: the public key uses an SPKI structure wrapped in PUBLIC KEY headers, and the private key uses a PKCS#8 structure wrapped in PRIVATE KEY headers.

faq.q: Are the generated keys intended for production use?
faq.a: The keys are produced with the browser's standard cryptographic generator, but they are best suited for testing, prototyping, and local development; evaluate your own security requirements before relying on browser-generated keys in production.

faq.q: Can I generate keys for encryption?
faq.a: The keys are generated for signing and verification (sign/verify usages). They are configured for signature algorithms (RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5 and ECDSA), not for encryption.
